chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Sulayman ibn Khalid, who said:

I asked Abu 'Abdillah عليه السلام about a man who forgot to sit in the first two rak'ahs. He said: If he remembers before he bows in ruku', then he should sit; but if he does not remember until he has bowed, then he should complete the salat (prayer), and when he has finished and given salām, he should perform the two sajdahs of forgetfulness.

key_terms.الرَّكْعَتَيْنِ الْأَوَّلَتَيْنِ: the first two units of salat (prayer)
key_terms.سَجْدَتَيِ السَّهْوِ: the two prostrations performed to remedy forgetfulness in prayer
key_terms.سَلَّمَ: to conclude the prayer with salām
key_terms.يَجْلِسَ: to sit for the required sitting of tashahhud in context

ai.seo_question: What should a person do if he forgets the first tashahhud in salat (prayer) and remembers after standing for the third rak'ah?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about one who forgets the first tashahhud in salat (prayer) until rising for the third rak'ah. If he remembers before entering ruku', he returns to sit; if he remembers only after ruku', he completes the salat (prayer) and then performs the two sajdahs of forgetfulness after salām.
